result.summary:
Independently re-derived from docs/agents/design/REQ-025.md (CODE-DESIGNER) and docs/agents/design/REQ-025-schema.md (DATA-DESIGNER) themselves -- not from either producer's step-01 result.summary -- against issue #28's six ACs, security-invariants.md S9/S10, decisions/0006-test-framework-vitest.md's actual text, and the live apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts.

1. ZERO IMPLEMENTATION CODE (exhaustive, both docs). Every function in REQ-025.md is a bare signature ending in `;` with no body (`sendLedgeredNotification(...): Promise<SendOutcome>;`, `createRateLimitedSender(...): NotificationSender;`, `startScheduledJobs(...): SchedulerHandle;`), interfaces/type unions only elsewhere (NotificationSender, SendNotificationInput, SendOutcome, NotificationKind, SendClassification, RateLimiterConfig, ScheduledJobDefinition, SchedulerHandle, UserForNotification). All branching logic (the ledger-insert-first ordering, the blocked/opt-in gates, the 429 backoff/retry/exhaustion behavior, the scheduler's overlap guard and failure isolation) is stated as prose rule tables (Sec3.1, Sec5, Sec7), exactly the discipline this role's own file mandates after the REQ-016/017 traps -- no if/return/arithmetic/comparison statement anywhere. The one inline composeMessage sketch in Sec4 point 3 ('...build the exact same [...] text as REQ-023 Sec6.3 already does...') is prose-with-ellipsis referencing pre-existing unchanged logic, not executable code. REQ-025-schema.md's Sec5 CREATE TABLE block is a literal single DDL statement transcribing Sec4's own column table into SQL syntax -- a structural declaration with no computation/branching, consistent with this project's own established, already-gated precedent (REQ-014-schema.md/REQ-019-schema.md's literal single-statement ALTER TABLE blocks); this is not implementation code in the sense the gate exists to catch (component/handler bodies with real logic), it is the same DDL-as-structure-restatement CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR has already passed twice before for this exact artefact type.

2. TOKEN REFERENCES. Both docs correctly state 'No design tokens apply' up front (bot/backend requirement, no rendered UI or copy surface). Scanned both files for any var(--...)/color/spacing/typography reference -- zero matches. Nothing to resolve against tokens.css; correctly N/A rather than silently skipped.

3. AC1 CRASH-WINDOW REASONING -- TRACED THE EXACT SCENARIO AND CONFIRMED CORRECT. Run 1: sendLedgeredNotification's step 4 INSERT into notification_ledger(registration_id, kind) commits, then step 5's sender.send(...) actually returns (message delivered). Process is killed. Run 2 (fresh process, fresh memory): the same job re-invokes sendLedgeredNotification with the identical (registrationId, kind). Step 1-3 gates re-evaluate the same way (no state consulted there is job-run-scoped). Step 4 attempts the same INSERT -- it now collides with the already-committed row from run 1 and Postgres raises unique-violation 23505 against UNIQUE(registration_id, kind), which Sec3.1 step 4 explicitly catches and converts to `{ kind: "skipped-already-sent" }`, returning **without ever reaching step 5's sender.send call**. So run 2 does not resend -- exactly one message is delivered across the kill+restart, which is precisely what AC1 literally tests. This is a DB-backed guard (survives the memory wipe), not an in-memory one, so it genuinely requires the two-process construction Sec3.3 names for TEST-DESIGNER. Separately and correctly, Sec3.2 names the crash-mid-window case (killed between step 4's commit and step 5's send actually completing) as a different, accepted-risk scenario (silent under-delivery, not a duplicate) that AC1's 'exactly one' wording does not test -- the document is explicit that the verification kill-point must be placed *after* the first run's send call has resolved, which is the right instruction for TEST-DESIGNER and correctly distinguishes the two scenarios rather than conflating them. The insert-before-send ordering is also the only one of the two possible orderings that cannot produce a genuine duplicate delivery (the reverse order's failure mode, send-then-crash-before-insert-commits, is a real duplicate -- S9's actual negative case); insert-then-send can only ever under-send, never over-send, which is the correct tradeoff given S9's stated harm ('messaging a real person repeatedly'). Confirmed sound.

4. `kind`-AS-`text` DECISION -- VERIFIED AGAINST THE LIVE SCHEMA. Read apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts lines 324-346 directly: `action: text("action").notNull()` and `entity: text("entity").notNull()` on audit_log are in fact plain `text` columns, not a pgEnum -- the cited precedent is real, not invented. The reasoning DATA-DESIGNER gives for applying it here (a value set stated in REQ-025.md Sec1 itself as growing roughly once per near-term requirement -- reminder_24h/reminder_3h/event_cancelled already named as landing in REQ-026/027, plus two Release-3 marketing kinds per S10 -- versus admission/event_status's genuinely-fixed, PRD-exhaustive sets that justify pgEnum per REQ-011.md Sec4) is the same shape of argument REQ-011.md Sec7 already made for audit_log.action/entity, applied to a structurally identical growing-set case. No AC (AC1-AC6) tests kind's DB-level closedness -- AC2 tests only the UNIQUE constraint via a direct duplicate-insert attempt, which text does not weaken in any way. Sound, and the missing-CHECK-constraint MINOR issue is resolved below.

5. `created_at: DEFAULT now()` DECISION -- VERIFIED AGAINST decisions/0006's ACTUAL TEXT, NOT ASSUMED FROM ITS TITLE. Read decisions/0006-test-framework-vitest.md's 'The boundary: fake timers do not reach Postgres' section directly (this is genuinely the record governing the evaluation-time-as-explicit-parameter rule despite its filename/title being about the Vitest choice -- confirmed the rule text lives there, at lines 90-116). It states the explicit-clock rule applies to 'any predicate whose truth depends on the current time' (WHERE ends_at < $1, no_show, registration_open) and then carves out, verbatim: 'This does not apply to audit/bookkeeping columns (created_at, updated_at, an AuditLog row's at) where a database default is correct and no test asserts on it.' notification_ledger.created_at is exactly this carved-out case: nothing in REQ-025.md's design (Sec1-Sec7) ever reads the ledger's timestamp back into a time-window comparison -- the table's only consumer is the UNIQUE(registration_id, kind) constraint itself. DATA-DESIGNER's framing (Sec3) is the correct reading of 0006's actual scope, not a misapplication. On the anticipated-future-need question (REQ-026/027 possibly wanting 'don't resend within N hours of the last send of this kind'): DATA-DESIGNER correctly does not pre-build this -- no AC1-AC6 asks for it today, and the schema doc's Sec3 closing paragraph and Sec7.2 already correctly state that if such a predicate is ever added, it must take an explicit $evaluation_time parameter per 0006 with created_at supplying the 'when it happened' side -- the column itself does not need to change shape to support that later, only the future query does. This is the right judgment: pre-emptively deviating from the audit-column carve-out today, for a predicate no acceptance criterion asks for, would be inventing a requirement, which this role is bound not to do.

6. TRANSACTIONAL/MARKETING SIGNATURE -- VERIFIED NO DEFAULT. Read Sec3's exact interface: `classification: SendClassification;` -- no `?`, no default value, on a type with exactly two members ('transactional' | 'marketing'). Every call site (Sec4's rewritten sendPromotionNotification, and every future call the interface allows) must supply it explicitly at the TypeScript level; there is no code path that could silently inherit a default. AC5 satisfied structurally.

7. 429/BACKOFF DESIGN -- VERIFIED CONCRETE AND TESTABLE. Sec5's rule table names the exact detection condition (GrammyError.error_code === 429, parameters.retry_after per Telegram's documented shape), the exact wait/retry mechanism (wait retry_after or initialBackoffMs, retry the same logical send), exact growth (double previous wait, capped at maxBackoffMs, up to maxRetries), exact exhaustion behavior (propagates as `{ kind: "failed", error }`, never an uncaught throw), and exact non-429 handling (no retry). Concrete default numbers are given (25/sec, 5 retries, 1000ms/30000ms backoff) so TEST-DESIGNER has fixed values to assert against. AC6's exact stub scenario (429 then 200, exactly one retry, message sent once at the Telegram-call level) is walked through explicitly. Not hand-wavy -- implementable and testable as written.

8. TWO FLAGGED MINOR ISSUES -- RESOLVED. (a) Citation mismatch: confirmed fixed. REQ-025.md Sec1 incorrectly claimed audit_log.at is caller-supplied; schema.ts line 339 shows `at: timestamp(...).notNull().defaultNow()` -- DATA-DESIGNER's Sec8 correction is accurate and its own design (Sec3) correctly follows the real precedent, not the misdescribed one. This is a documentation-accuracy defect confined to REQ-025.md's citation text; it does not affect any functional design element (no design decision in either document actually depends on which way that citation read), so it is non-blocking for Step 1b -- carried forward as the same MINOR severity DATA-DESIGNER already recorded, not escalated. (b) Missing DB CHECK on `kind`'s closed set: DATA-DESIGNER's reasoning accepted, not overridden -- no AC tests DB-level enum enforcement, the sole write path is already compile-time-checked against the NotificationKind union at its one call site, and a CHECK would reintroduce a recurring per-value migration cost for the same reason pgEnum was rejected, consistent with this schema's own chapters.code/users.role/audit_log.action precedent of carrying no CHECK either.

9. AC-TO-DESIGN-ELEMENT MAP -- re-derived against issue #28's six ACs, not trusted from either document's own Sec9 table. AC1 (two-process restart, exactly one send) -> item 3 above. AC2 (git grep finds no in-memory record; DB UNIQUE enforced, verified by direct duplicate insert) -> REQ-025-schema.md Sec4 'Keys / uniqueness' (a real Postgres UNIQUE constraint, Sec1's own explicit claim that no Set/Map/module-level tracker appears anywhere in Sec2/Sec3/Sec5/Sec7 of REQ-025.md was checked directly -- confirmed, no such construct appears in either document). AC3 (transactional-vs-marketing respects broadcast_opt_in) -> Sec3.1 step 3 (broadcastOptIn read only when classification==="marketing"; never read for "transactional"). AC4 (blocked=true skips both) -> Sec3.1 step 2 (unconditional check preceding the classification branch). AC5 (no default on classification) -> item 6 above. AC6 (429 triggers backoff-retry, exactly-once delivery) -> item 7 above. All six map to concrete, non-deferred design elements across the two documents combined; open questions in both (REQ-025.md Sec8, REQ-025-schema.md Sec7) are each named explicitly with an owner or explicit non-goal, never a silent gap in an AC-relevant area.

Verdict: PASS. No check failed. Both artefacts gated together as required by WF-02 Step 0.9's bot-requirement rule.

issues.description: docs/agents/design/REQ-025.md Sec1 misdescribes the audit_log.at precedent, claiming the ledger's 'moment sent' value must be caller-supplied 'matching this schema's decisions/0006... discipline already applied to audit_log.at.' Verified directly against apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts line 339: audit_log.at is in fact `defaultNow()`, not caller-supplied. docs/agents/design/REQ-025-schema.md Sec8 already caught and corrected this citation, and its own design (created_at DEFAULT now()) correctly follows the real precedent rather than the misdescribed one -- so no functional design element in either document actually depends on the incorrect citation. Non-blocking for Step 1b. Recommend DOC-UPDATER or a future touch of REQ-025.md correct Sec1's citation text for accuracy, but no rework of either design artefact is required before Step 2.

No DB-level CHECK(kind IN (...)) constraint on notification_ledger.kind. DATA-DESIGNER's reasoning (REQ-025-schema.md Sec2, Sec7.1) is accepted as-is, not overridden: no acceptance criterion tests DB-level closedness of `kind` (AC2 tests only the UNIQUE constraint), the sole write path is already compile-time-checked against the NotificationKind union at its one call site (sendLedgeredNotification), and a CHECK would reintroduce a recurring per-value migration cost -- consistent with this schema's existing chapters.code/users.role/audit_log.action precedent of carrying no CHECK either. Recorded here per the handoff's instruction to confirm/override; confirmed, no override.
